svg.title: Expectation index: the finite-level trace excludes the gaps
svg.desc: A faithful normal expectation between sigma-finite factors produces a tower with index d and finite-level Markov traces. Recursive projections have trace a(n+1) divided by delta to the n. The first negative value excludes non-discrete indices below four. Separate path and tensor constructions realize all allowed values.

g.text: Index restrictions without a trace on the ambient factors
E : M → N faithful and normal; M, N sigma-finite factors; d = Idx(E)
δ = √d, a₀ = 0, a₁ = 1, aₙ₊₁ = δaₙ − aₙ₋₁
fₙ is a projection using denominators a₂, …, aₙ; τ(fₙ) = aₙ₊₁ / δⁿ
If d < 4 and d ≠ 4 cos²(π/r), some defined fₙ would have negative trace.
Exact example: d = 3/2 ⇒ a₂, a₃ > 0 but τ(f₃) = −1/3. Impossible.
Necessity: positivity above. Realization: earlier programme path inclusions;
identity at d = 1; P ⊗ 1 ⊂ P ⊗ P at d = ∞. The interval includes infinity.
Proof locators: EIR01–02 (tower and trace), EIR03–04 (recursion and gaps), EIR05–06 (realization and example).
